rubrics.criterion: The restructured code has no remaining function that carries a whole multi-level helper chain in one body: in each of the six fused areas (the single-test command, the shared formatter pipeline, the import-sorting command, the inlay-hints provider, the flake8 provider's run method, and the document diagnostics engine), the outer function delegates the absorbed steps back to single-purpose helper methods, and no replacement function approaches the original fused bodies' combined size, nesting, or mixing of unrelated concerns (process plumbing, tool resolution, diff decoding, result mapping inside one body).
rubrics.rationale: This is the defining outcome of the assigned over-inlining problem: the six site-specific fused bodies are the injected defect. The rubric judges the structural destination on each named responsibility (any sound decomposition qualifies — extracted helpers, shared-service delegation, or a mix), not any specific method names, signatures, or a specific prior layout.

rubrics.criterion: The unified-diff decoding logic (turning an external tool's diff output into text edits for a document: hunk-header parsing, per-sign line processing, insert/delete/replace application with correct start-position resets) exists in exactly one place again, shared by both the formatter pipeline and the import-sorting flow — neither keeps a private divergent copy.
rubrics.rationale: The two reworked inline decoders (in the formatter base pipeline and the import-sorting command) are deliberate divergent duplicates of the codebase's diff-decode utility; deduplicating them across two distinct callers is the single highest-value re-ownership move in this instance and requires recognizing algorithmically equal but stylistically different code.

rubrics.criterion: Generic (tool-agnostic) framework paths read external-tool settings dynamically per tool id again: whichever component resolves a tool's executable path, enabled flag, extra arguments, or stdin preference does so through id-derived or provider-descriptor-driven lookups, with no tool-id spelled into a literal setting key (e.g. no literal `flake8...`-prefixed settings keys, no formatter-id literals in the formatter base) in code intended to serve all tools.
rubrics.rationale: The flake8 site replaced dynamic per-provider descriptor reads (the provider-info object holding id-derived setting keys and default arguments) with era-specific literal keys, and the case's prompt explicitly requires generic paths to stay generic. Restoring dynamic lookup is a distinct semantic outcome from mere extraction and is checkable independent of the decomposition chosen.

rubrics.criterion: Per-tool component construction goes back through a factory/registry-style seam: given a tool enumeration, the diagnostics engine (and any other generic caller) obtains the matching provider through one construction pathway (factory method, registry, or equivalent) rather than via an inlined type/switch statement inside the calling method.
rubrics.rationale: The diagnostics engine's construction switch was created by absorbing its own factory method. The semantic outcome — construction knowledge owned by one seam — admits several implementations and is what keeps a future provider from needing edits in every call site.

rubrics.criterion: The flake8 provider delegates again to the shared provider machinery for the work that machinery already owns (process execution, stdout/stderr handling, line-protocol message decoding, severity mapping): the provider contributes only what is actually flake8-specific (its format arguments, its settings, its column-offset behavior), and no divergent copy of the shared decoding/severity pipeline remains in the flake8 module.
rubrics.rationale: This site inlines a chain into a body while the original chain stays alive for nine sibling providers, so the repair must restore delegation to the retained shared code rather than deleting seams. It is the clearest duplication-vs-deletion discriminator in the instance.

rubrics.criterion: Test-function discovery for the single-test command is owned by a reusable, single-purpose traversal of the parsed tree (a walker/helper that enumerates test functions and reconstructs suite-qualified names), instead of the command hand-rolling recursive descent, parser construction, and probe steps inline; and the interpreter/framework validation probes (version and module existence) are performed through a shared helper rather than duplicated in the command.
rubrics.rationale: The command absorbed three levels of the parser module (parse facade, framework walker, tree-node utilities) plus its sibling dial-up helper. Restoration of a named discovery/traversal owner (existing parser-module walker reconstituted, a new helper, or reuse of the dial-up helper) is independently gradable without fixing exact names.

rubrics.criterion: The inlay-hints provider delegates again: configuration-driven hint-kind filtering, hover/signature requests racing a timeout, and the three per-kind label conversions (variable/return/parameter) each live in focused single-purpose units (methods or helpers), and the provider's main method no longer computes range membership or protocol-request plumbing inline.
rubrics.rationale: This site is the many-tiny-helpers shape of the same defect: the semantic intermediate concepts (what forms each hint kind) were fused into one provider loop. Re-splitting them by kind is the material outcome here.

rubrics.criterion: Every seam that sibling implementations rely on still works through the repaired shared code: the formatter that overrides content staging still exerts its override through the shared pipeline (its special staging actually used when that formatter id runs), and the shared provider base classes and their overridable methods continue to serve the sibling providers that subclass them.
rubrics.rationale: The fused formatter pipeline deliberately kept its staging seam as a call; a solver who dissolves the seam or specializes the base would break the overriding formatter — the sharpest hidden-coupling trap in this instance. This is the associated change that must accompany the formatter decomposition.

rubrics.criterion: Re-extracted helpers are placed with a coherent owner: infrastructural pieces (executable/module resolution, process execution and output decoding, diff decoding, positioning utilities) sit in the shared layers or utilities where the codebase already keeps such logic, while tool- or feature-specific behavior stays in the responsible feature or provider class — the repair does not deposit generic machinery inside feature command bodies nor duplicate provider data access in the shared layers.
rubrics.rationale: Deep over-inlining repair is not just about shrinking bodies but about returning each responsibility to its natural module; the codebase has a clear shared/utility-vs-feature/provider split, and misplaced extraction would leave the same maintenance problem in a different shape.

rubrics.criterion: Feature paths that were healthy before the fused era keep their behavior without having to carry duplicated copies: the whole-file test command routes through the same shared test dial-up logic as the single-test path (or through one equivalent shared implementation), rather than keeping a second divergent copy of the probe/terminal logic.
rubrics.rationale: The original dial-up helper remains because the whole-file command uses it; reusing (or merging into one) shared dial-up end state is the natural associated change that completes the test-runner cluster without demanding one specific layout.

rubrics.criterion: Era debris introduced only to support the inlined bodies is fully removed: any module-level constant, named-capture regex string, local interface/type, or local helper (e.g. severity-mapping closures, flush/report procedures, temp-name builders, block/record types for inline diff replay) that served the fused implementations is deleted or folded into a single shared owner — nothing equivalent survives unused in a module that also delegates to the shared implementation.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that restores delegation but leaves the now-orphaned scaffolding behind keeps every readable path doubling itself; the literal regex/interface/state-machine debris is the direct residue of this instance's injection and its removal is independently observable.

rubrics.criterion: Import statements and module dependencies end up consistent with the repaired code: no imports exist that are used only by removed inline code (e.g. node built-ins or hash/path/child-process pieces pulled in solely for the absorbed plumbing), and no new import of a module is kept merely to re-implement it elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: Deep absorption dragged process, path, hashing, and os imports into feature modules that never needed them at this layer; tracking those back is part of making the repaired modules coherent rather than merely smaller.

rubrics.criterion: For some supported tool id, generic configuration handling regresses: a tool's configured executable path, extra arguments, enabled flag, or stdin preference stops being honored for that id (e.g. because a generic path reads a literal key of another id, or because the provider lost access to its settings descriptor), so behavior for at least one id depends on the wrong setting.
rubrics.rationale: The most plausible over-fitting failure in this instance is repairing the structure while hard-wiring what were dynamic id-derived lookups — the case deliberately flipped those to era literals, and a solver who keeps the literals (or generalizes them wrongly) changes behavior for every other id silently for all tools but one.

rubrics.criterion: Message or diagnostic decoding drifts for the affected provider: flake8 findings lose their row-column semantics (e.g. the zero-or-negative-column clamp, the dedicated column offset, or the exit-zero handling that tolerates its nonzero exits), or the engine's message-to-diagnostic conversion changes positions/severities (e.g. the quote-based column repositioning for findings surfaced by the engine, or unknown-severity fallbacks), producing different diagnostics than before for the same tool output.
rubrics.rationale: These decoding subtleties are the invisible behavioral payload inside the inlined chains; a re-implementation from a reading (rather than faithful relocation) of the fused code plausibly drops exactly these, and each is directly observable in the resulting diagnostics for the same simulated tool output.

rubrics.criterion: Temp-file handling regresses: a staged sidecar file remains on disk after a tool exits or fails (unlinked in fewer paths than before), the file is placed somewhere other than beside the user's source (breaking tools that resolve neighboring configs), a cleanup path double-runs, or an implementation deletes/overwrites the user's original document.
rubrics.rationale: Both the formatter pipeline and the import-sorting command stage a file next to the document with explicit leak-on-early-failure and unlink-on-teardown semantics; the fused versions preserved them (a maintenance accident here is invisible to the static gate), and repairs that move staging into a helper can quietly change when deletion happens.

rubrics.criterion: Cancellation behavior breaks in the formatter flow: a cancelled token during a run lets the tool's edits still be reported/applied, yields an error presented to the user instead of a quiet early return, or leaves the staged file behind when cancellation previously guaranteed cleanup.
rubrics.rationale: The fused pipeline threads cancellation before/after execution and on the error path with dedicated efforts; re-splitting the flow is where cancellation ordering most plausibly slips, and each listed deviation is user-visible without any tool misbehaving.

rubrics.criterion: Test selection or invocation changes: discovered test items include non-test functions or exclude valid ones, suite-qualified name reconstruction uses the wrong separator between the two supported frameworks, the previously used terminal is not disposed (buffers pile up), or the invocation transcript sent to the terminal composes a different command for the same document/test.
rubrics.rationale: The fused test-runner replaced the framework walker with manual descent; each of these failures is a concrete way a rewritten traversal/invocation diverges from the walker-based behavior for the same source, and they are all observable from the resulting discovery and terminal activity.

rubrics.criterion: Inlay-hint output changes for at least one hint kind: hints appear at wrong positions for variable/return/parameter kinds, the parameter hint excludes or includes the wrong parameters (e.g. no longer filtering reserved-dunder names or missing the suffix convention), the 200ms response timeout stops limiting hover/signature requests, or hint kinds silently stop appearing for other configured users.
rubrics.rationale: The label conversions encode non-obvious rules (return-type text slicing, dunder filtering, variable-kind exclusion of definitions) that a from-scratch rewrite of the fused provider loop plausibly alters; the failures are observable in hint output per kind.
